title: How does a drive-through know when your car arrives?

lines.text: The moment your front bumper pulls up to a fast-food ordering menu, a chime beeps inside the employee's headset.
lines.caps: How does a drive-through *know | the second you pull *up?

lines.text: It is not a cashier staring out the window or a hidden camera triggering the chime.
lines.caps: Not a camera or *employee | watching the *window!

lines.text: Buried beneath the asphalt pavement is an induction loop sensor made of insulated copper wire.
lines.caps: Buried under the pavement is an *inductive | copper wire *loop

lines.text: An electrical current runs through the wire loop, creating an invisible electromagnetic field above the driveway.
lines.caps: Creates an invisible *electromagnetic | field above the *ground

lines.text: When thousands of pounds of steel in your car roll overhead, the metal disrupts the coil's magnetic inductance.
lines.caps: Your car's steel *disrupts | the magnetic field's *frequency

lines.text: The detector registers the frequency shift, triggering the headset chime and starting an automated order timer.
lines.caps: Triggers the headset *chime | and starts a customer *timer!

lines.text: That buried magnetic sensor keeps fast-food drive-through lines moving at lightning speed.
lines.caps: Buried magnetic loops *powering | millions of fast-food *orders!
